# Report on `region.fasta` (region_006)

**Sequence: 3,000 nt (plus strand), GC 54.9%** (C 883, G 764, T 702, A 651). All coordinates below are 1-based, inclusive, on the plus strand.

## Main finding: the region is clearly protein-coding — two long, convergent ORFs covering 84% of it

| | ORF-A (plus strand) | ORF-B (minus strand) |
|---|---|---|
| Location | **328–1332** | **1484–2992** (minus-strand nt 9–1517) |
| Start / stop | TTG at 328–330 / TAA at 1330–1332 | GTG at 2990–2992 (minus 9–11) / TAG at 1484–1486 (minus 1515–1517) |
| Size | 1005 nt → **334 aa** (~37.6 kDa) | 1509 nt → **502 aa** (~54.7 kDa) |
| Properties | pI ≈ 11.2, GRAVY +0.29 | pI ≈ 5.0, GRAVY ≈ 0, no TM |
| Composition | Phe-rich (43 F = 12.9%), Arg 8.7% | Leu 13.5%; Arg 6.6% vs Lys 2.6%; CTG used 40× |

**Evidence these are real genes, not chance ORFs:** both frames are stop-free over 335 and 503 codons respectively, while the two off-frames *within the same segments* carry 10–26 stops (3–5 per 100 codons) — i.e., ~11 and ~22 stops would be expected. Both also show classic coding-potential signatures: **GC3 = 64.2% / 62.2% vs GC12 = 49.9% / 54.4%**, and GC-biased codon usage (CTG, GCG, GGC, GGT dominant).

**ORF-A looks membrane-associated:** a hydrophobic, Phe-rich segment at aa 34–88 (**nt 427–591**), with 19-aa windows peaking at GRAVY +2.5 (aa 66–84) — consistent with one or two transmembrane helices — plus a weaker hydrophobic patch at the C-terminus (aa ~311–334, nt 1258–1329). It is simultaneously highly basic (pI 11.2). ORF-B looks like a soluble cytosolic protein (no TM, near-neutral hydropathy).

## Layout

The two genes are **convergent**, their 3′ ends facing an **AT-rich intergenic gap at 1333–1483** (151 nt, 42.4% GC vs 54.9% overall). ORF-B's start codon sits only 8 nt from the right edge of the fragment (only 2993–3000 lies 5′ of it), so its promoter/RBS must lie outside the captured region — this looks like an interior slice of a larger locus. The 327 nt upstream of ORF-A (52.6% GC) contains only small, likely incidental ORFs (largest: GTG 136 → TAA 298–300, 54 aa).

## Accessory signals — remarkably few

- **No promoters:** no −35 (TTGACA) / −10 (TATAAT) pair on either strand even allowing one mismatch each at 15–19 nt spacing; no TGn extended −10.
- **No clear ribosome-binding sites:** no AGGAGG/GGAGG-type core within 15 nt upstream of either gene's start (the only GGAGG motifs, at 1207 and 2792, precede no start codon). Alternative in-frame starts exist (ORF-A: GTG at 550, 598 — the latter has an SD-like GGGAT at 593–597; ORF-B: nested GTG/ATG, e.g. ATG at plus 2462–2464 and 2210–2212 with purine-rich leaders), so translation starts are ambiguous without homology data.
- **No canonical rho-independent terminator:** the best hairpin in the entire 3 kb is only a 6-bp stem (GGATTG·CAATCC, loop TACC) at **1441–1456**, followed 7 nt later by a T₆ run at **1463–1468** — a possible weak terminator-like element ~110 nt 3′ of ORF-A's stop (for ORF-B the same structure sits ~30 nt downstream but the run is A-rich, not U-rich, on its mRNA).
- **Almost no repeats:** the only exact repeat ≥12 nt is a 13-mer, **GAATGCGATTATT at 1360–1372** (in the intergenic gap) and **2479–2491** (inside ORF-B, codons 168–171); everything else is ≤11 nt (background level). Palindromic hexamers are if anything depleted (35 observed vs ~48 expected).
- **One notable palindrome:** a perfect 8-bp-stem/8-nt-loop hairpin at **2938–2961** (CCAGCACG…CGTGCTGG), inside ORF-B near its 5′ end (aa 12–20) — the only strong secondary-structure element in the region.
- Homopolymer tracts: T₆ 1463–1468; T₅ 482–486, 1066–1070, 2387–2391; A₅ 2601–2605; C₅ 1325–1329 (encodes the T–P at ORF-A's C-terminus), 1742–1746, 2782–2786 (the latter two give Gly/Pro clusters in ORF-B).

## Ruled out

- No tRNA-like cloverleaf structures or rRNA-conserved oligos (tRNA/rRNA 16S/23S/5S motif scans).
- No CRISPR arrays, tandem repeats, or mobile-element/att-site features.
- Restriction sites are unremarkable: 13 of 21 common 6-cutters present as single, scattered copies (e.g., EcoRI GAATTC at 127–132), 13 observed vs ~17 expected — no enrichment, so not a cloning/MCS artifact. GATC (Dam) sites also at expected frequency.

## Bottom line

This is **not** a featureless sequence: it is a coding locus. Its notable content is two substantial, convergent bacterial-style protein-coding genes — a 334-aa, basic, Phe-rich, putatively membrane-spanning protein (plus strand, 328–1332) and a 502-aa soluble protein (minus strand, 1484–2992) — separated by an AT-rich intergenic gap (1333–1483), together spanning 84% of the fragment. Regulatory DNA (promoters, RBSs, terminators), repeats, and structural RNAs are essentially absent within the captured 3 kb, implying the regulatory elements lie outside the fragment's edges. No recognizable catalytic or family motif is present in either protein, and with no database available offline I cannot assign a function by homology — identifying what these genes encode would require a BLAST/HMMER search against known proteins.
